title: M11 - Cost tracking and attribution
description:
Auritus has a daily AWS Budget and a kill-switch, but no idea what anything
costs. The budget is an account-wide blunt instrument: it fires at a dollar
threshold and disables the Batch queue. Nothing attributes spend to a job, a
site, or a backend, and nothing distinguishes the free path from the paid one.

That gap undercuts the product's central claim. Auritus exists so a publisher
can run synthesis on a GPU they control and pay AWS nothing; the local worker
races the cloud fallback precisely to avoid GPU spend. We cannot currently
show that this works.

## What already exists

More than it appears. Per-job cost is tractable today because:

- `_claim_job` records `worker_type` as `local` or `batch`
- The Batch runner claims as `f"batch:{AWS_BATCH_JOB_ID}"`
  (`worker-image/src/runner.py:117`), so **the AWS Batch job ID is already
  stored** in `claimed_by` -- the join key to real billing data
- The compute environment is a single fixed instance type (`g4dn.xlarge`),
  EC2 on-demand, no Spot, `maxv_cpus=8` -- at most two concurrent instances
  of one known rate, with no instance-type mix to model
- `duration_seconds` is recorded per job

## Approach: hybrid

Per-job **estimates** from a rate card, for attribution and immediacy, plus a
daily **actual** from Cost Explorer displayed beside the summed estimate. The
delta between them calibrates the rate card and is itself useful information.

Estimates alone drift silently. Cost Explorer alone cannot answer "what did
this clip, or this site, cost" -- per-job cost allocation tags are impractical
at job cardinality. Neither half is sufficient.

## Two accuracy traps

**Container runtime is not billed time.** `duration_seconds` is
`completed_at - claimed_at`. With `minv_cpus=0` every cold start bills for EC2
boot, ECS agent registration, and a multi-gigabyte GPU image pull before the
container ever claims a job. On a cold start that overhead can exceed the
synthesis. Billed seconds must come from Batch's own `startedAt`/`stoppedAt`
plus a provisioning allowance -- not from our claim timestamps.

**Instance time is shared.** Two concurrent jobs on one `g4dn.xlarge` must not
each be charged the full hourly rate. Per-job cost has to amortize across
whatever else ran on that instance.

## Local is not free

DynamoDB, Lambda, S3 storage, and CloudFront egress bill on every job
regardless of who synthesized it. Small, but a console that prints "$0.00" for
local jobs states something false. Report GPU cost and platform cost as
separate lines throughout.

## Aggregation cannot ride on the current scan

`_get_admin_overview` computes its KPIs from `_jobs.scan(Limit=100)`. That is
already the defect behind auritus-294fa6, where a 25-item page silently
omitted the newest job in the system. Cost totals derived that way would be
confidently wrong rather than visibly incomplete. Rollups are written on
completion, never scanned at read time.

## Order of work

```mermaid
graph TD
  A[Batch billing telemetry] --> B[Per-job estimated cost]
  B --> C[Daily cost rollups]
  B --> D[Local worker savings]
  C --> E[Cost Explorer reconciliation]
  C --> F[Costs in the CLI]
  C --> G[Costs in the web console]
  D --> F
  D --> G
```

comments.text:
Phase A production verification complete (2026-09-16). Full wipe of pre-existing
27 jobs, recreated across the matrix:

- Local-worker path (demo site a83f51e6): kokoro x2, qwen x1, all completed via
  a real local worker after fixing a corrupted torch install (missing
  libtorch_cpu.dylib -- unrelated environment issue, not a code bug). Rollup:
  gpu_cost_usd=$0, platform_cost_usd=$0.0025, avoided_cost_usd=$0.0175,
  job_count=5 (includes 2 transient failures before retry, correctly counted).

- AWS Batch path (new dedicated test site 50ae9519): chatterbox + higgs,
  deliberately left unclaimed by any local worker, correctly fell through the
  900s Step Functions fallback and completed via real Batch jobs. Rollup:
  gpu_cost_usd=$0.0277 (nonzero, from real batch_telemetry), platform_cost_usd
  =$0.0010, avoided_cost_usd=$0 (correctly suppressed), avoided_cost_basis=
  batch_job on both.

- Per-site isolation confirmed: `auritus cost --site <test_site> --daily`
  returns only that site's 2 jobs, cleanly separated from the demo site's
  rollup.

Found and fixed one real production bug in the process (auritus-d62743,
already closed): the M10/M11 admin routes were never wired to API Gateway.

Not verifiable same-day: Cost Explorer reconciliation (auritus-c56c4a's
cost_reconciliation Lambda) -- Cost Explorer data isn't final for ~24h and
the Lambda only reconciles days closed that long ago. Follow up tomorrow
(2026-09-17) with `auritus cost --daily` to confirm a reconciled row appears
for 2026-09-16 with `actual_cost_usd` populated and close to the $0.0277 +
$0.0035 estimated total.
